post.description:
Import browser-local records into the tenant's backend store.

`legacyKey` that is already stored is reported as skipped, never
re-created. Unknown sections are rejected rather than silently filed under a
guess, and legacy keys the schema does not model are preserved under
``metadata.legacyFields`` instead of breaking the insert.

Idempotency is enforced by a UNIQUE index on (account_id, legacy_key), so a
second run reports `skipped` rather than duplicating. An entry with no
legacy key is always created, because there is no way to tell it apart from
a genuinely new check.

post.description:
Fork (rewind) a session â the Claude-Code snapshot pattern, made honest.

A NEW session copies every message up to and including `upto_message_id`
(or all messages when omitted). The parent session is NEVER mutated, so a
rewind can never lose work; the child records its lineage in
`chat_session_forks`.

get.description:
The session's plan graph (prompt â tool steps â answer), reconstructed.

Built from the recorded tool-call ledger + message parts. Linear and honest:
nothing is invented beyond what ran.

Every build artifact attached to a session, with ds_assets metadata.

Four different "it is not there" situations used to collapse into one broken
thumbnail, so the workbench could not tell the operator which one happened:

  missing_asset    - the attachment points at an asset row that no longer exists
  missing_metadata - the row exists but has no storage_key (nothing to serve)
  missing_file     - the row and key exist but the backing file is gone
  ok               - row + file present

`present` keeps its historical meaning (the asset ROW exists) because other
callers depend on it; `file_present`/`state` are the honest new detail.
An asset owned by another account is refused by get_by_id and therefore reads
as missing_asset - the same 404 posture as the file route.

post.description:
Guarded single-ASIN DataForSEO Standard-queue cross-check.

This is the ONLY route that may touch the DataForSEO adapter, and it
is fail-closed:

- DATAFORSEO_ENABLED must be an explicit opt-in (feature flag, false
  by default). Otherwise returns 403 and never touches a provider.
- An explicit one-run approval token must be supplied in the POST body
  (never a GET, never a UI toggle, never a page load). The token must
  equal the approval_run_id exactly.
- The candidate must have passed the internal shortlist logic; the
  contract rejects batches/lists/wildcards/keyword searches.
- The live transport is armed only by an explicit runtime opt-in:
  DATAFORSEO_TRANSPORT_ENABLED exactly "true" plus configured
  DATAFORSEO_LOGIN/DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD credentials. Without the arm,
  even a fully authorized request refuses before any network call
  (LIVE_CALLS_MADE=0); with the arm, the guarded Standard-queue
  submission runs with the budget ledger enforced.

GET routes and normal page loads never invoke this adapter.
